title: 1-D tolerance stack-up (worst-case + RSS) and bore/shaft fit check at printer extremes

governing_equations.name: nominal gap
governing_equations.description: Linear dimension chain: each element contributes its nominal n_i with sign dir_i (+1 adds to the gap, -1 consumes it).

governing_equations.name: worst-case (arithmetic) band
governing_equations.expr: g_min = g_nom - sum_i lo_i ;  g_max = g_nom + sum_i hi_i ;  hi_i = plus_i if dir_i=+1 else minus_i ;  lo_i = minus_i if dir_i=+1 else plus_i
governing_equations.description: Every element simultaneously at its unfavourable extreme, taken about the TRUE nominal (no mid-shift). For symmetric tolerances this is g_nom +/- sum_i t_i — the textbook worst-case stack.

governing_equations.name: RSS (statistical) band
governing_equations.expr: g_rss = g_nom + sum_i dir_i (plus_i - minus_i)/2 ;  sigma_g = sqrt( sum_i ((plus_i + minus_i)/2 / 3)^2 ) ;  band = g_rss +/- 3 sigma_g
governing_equations.description: Each asymmetric tolerance is first converted to the equivalent bilateral (standard mid-shift of the nominal by (plus-minus)/2, t_eq = (plus+minus)/2); each +/-t_eq is treated as a 3-sigma band of an independent normal contributor, so the gap sigma is the root-sum-square of t_eq_i/3. For symmetric tolerances: g_nom +/- sqrt(sum_i t_i^2).

governing_equations.name: fit extremes
governing_equations.expr: c_min = (bore_nom - bore_minus) - (shaft_nom + shaft_plus) ;  c_max = (bore_nom + bore_plus) - (shaft_nom - shaft_minus) ;  interference = c_min < 0
governing_equations.description: Smallest bore against the largest shaft, and the largest bore against the smallest shaft. An omitted tolerance takes printer_tol_default (0.15 mm, typical well-tuned FDM).

governing_equations.name: contributor ranking
governing_equations.expr: band_contribution_i = plus_i + minus_i ;  pct_of_band_i = 100 * band_contribution_i / sum_j band_contribution_j
governing_equations.description: Share of the worst-case band WIDTH each element owns, so the element to tighten first is the first row.

assumptions: The chain is one-dimensional and linear: every element lies along one axis and enters the gap with sign +/-1 — no angular, projected, or form-tolerance contributions.
Worst-case assumes all extremes can coincide (no correlation assumed, no probability claimed) — it is a guaranteed bound, not a likely outcome.

RSS assumes independent contributors whose +/-t are 3-sigma bands of normal distributions (process centred on the mid-shifted nominal, ~99.73% inside the band); it says nothing about a batch printed off-centre.
Printer tolerance defaults (0.15 mm) are a typical desktop-FDM figure — verify against YOUR printer's calibration; the tool does no measurement.
Pure arithmetic: no geometry, no engine calls, no physics.

boundary_conditions.fixtures: not applicable — the 'boundary' of a stack is its functional limit `closes` {min_required, max_allowed}; either side may be omitted (one-sided) and the receipt records which sides were checked.
boundary_conditions.selector_count_unit: chain elements (each element = one nominal + one tolerance)

inputs.chain[].tol: mm (+/-t) or {plus, minus} magnitudes in mm

discretization.element: none — exact arithmetic over the chain; results rounded to 9 decimals in the receipt
discretization.notes: No iteration, no mesh, no random sampling (no Monte Carlo).

additional_pins: tools/tests/test_checkers.py (gate suite: asymmetric double-count regression, one-sided closes, refusals)
validation.ground_truth: Hand-derived textbook stacks, arithmetic stated in the pin: 3-element chain 20.0+/-0.2 - 12.0+/-0.1 - 7.5+/-0.15 -> nominal 0.5, worst-case 0.5 +/- 0.45 = [0.05, 0.95], RSS 0.5 +/- sqrt(0.2^2+0.1^2+0.15^2) = 0.5 +/- 0.269258 = [0.230742, 0.769258]; asymmetric element 10 +0/-0.10 mid-shifts the RSS nominal by -0.05 while the worst-case band stays about the true nominal; fit 8.2+/-0.15 vs 8.0+/-0.15 -> clearance [-0.10, +0.50] (interference at extremes); the worst-case-fails-while-RSS-passes case that is the textbook reason RSS exists.

error_band.determinism: stdout receipt byte-identical across reruns (no clock fields) — measured identical

validation.direction: no bias — closed-form arithmetic; worst-case is a guaranteed (conservative) bound, RSS is a 3-sigma statistical band that is NARROWER than worst-case by construction.

caveats: 1-D only: it cannot see angular stack-ups, form errors, or datum shift; a real assembly with a tilted mating face needs a projected chain the user builds by hand.
RSS is only as honest as its independence + normality assumptions; a printer whose whole batch runs 0.1 mm large violates both — use worst-case for anything that must never bind.
pass_rss true with pass_worst false is a STATISTICAL pass: state that a fraction of assemblies (~0.27% per 3-sigma side, if the assumptions hold) will fall outside the band.
The 0.15 mm printer default is a stand-in for a measurement, not a measurement.
A failing verdict exits 2 with `ok:false` and `error_kind` 'internal' (the shared receipt contract's default slug for a gate failure); refusals carry `refusal.*` kinds.

limits_of_validity.regime: linear 1-D chains and bore/shaft pairs with bilateral or unilateral +/- tolerances; up to any number of elements
limits_of_validity.resolution: receipt values are rounded to 9 decimals (1 nm); tolerances below that are meaningless for FDM anyway

sources.title: Fischer, B.R., Mechanical Tolerance Stackup and Analysis, 2nd ed., CRC Press, 2011
sources.ref: ISBN 978-1-4398-1572-4 — worst-case (arithmetic) and statistical (RSS) stackup chapters; equal-bilateral conversion of unequal-bilateral tolerances (the mid-shift)
